question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees get 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays, which are not automatically taken as leave and must be booked like any other day. Employees with 3 years' continuous service get 1 extra day (29 in total), and those with 5 years get 2 extra days (30 in total), which is the maximum entitlement. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on their contracted hours.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly on the last working day of the month, according to the Employee Handbook (§5 Pay). Payslips are available in StaffHub.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: The standard probation period for new employees is 6 months, with manager review meetings at 3 months and 6 months. Probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed. During probation the notice period on either side is 1 week.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: If you use your own car for work, mileage is paid at 45p per mile (Expenses Policy §3). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, according to section 4 of the Information Security Policy (v2025.1). The IT Acceptable Use Policy (section 7) requires employees to follow these same password rules.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days, according to the Customer Complaints Procedure (v2025.1, effective 1 Jun 2025), §5 Timescales. The final response must be sent within 8 weeks.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: If you have between 3 and 5 years' service and have completed probation, you get 4 weeks of company sick pay at full pay in any rolling 12-month period. Company sick pay tops up Statutory Sick Pay to full basic pay.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Employees who have passed probation can apply for study support for a qualification relevant to their role. It covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications are made through LearnHub and must be approved by the line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing, you must repay 100% of the course fees; if you leave between 12 and 24 months after it finishes, you must repay 50%.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes. Under the Training and Development Policy, if you leave between 12 and 24 months after your course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. Leaving 18 months after the course finished falls in this band, so you would repay 50%. The passages do not state the exact amount in pounds, and they do not say how the repayment is collected from your final pay.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll (Remote and Workplace Policy §4). Employees must also use a company laptop and the company VPN when working remotely (§5).

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes, you can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year without needing approval. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, and any not used by then are lost and not paid. Carrying forward more than 8 days is only allowed in limited exceptions (long-term sickness, certain family leave, or manager-cancelled approved leave with written approval from the Head of People), in which case up to 20 days may be carried forward; sickness-related days must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year they were earned, while other exceptional days must be used by 30 June. The passages do not say how casual or zero-hours workers carry forward leave beyond their accrual rules.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately, since you have already clicked a link. You should also not click any further links or open attachments in the suspicious email, and use the Report Phish button in Outlook to report the email. The IT Service Desk can be contacted through StaffHub or on extension 4357.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. All tips given to gaming employees are placed in the tronc box at the table and shared through the tronc scheme (Code of Conduct §3). Hospitality employees follow their own venue's tipping process instead.

question: I'm too poorly to work my shift on the casino floor. How early do I need to ring in?
expected_answer: At least 2 hours before the shift starts, by phone to the line manager or duty manager.
ai_answer: Gaming floor, security and cage employees must phone their line manager or the duty manager at least 2 hours before the start of their shift, so cover can be arranged. Do not text or email unless you cannot speak. You must also call again each day you are absent unless your manager agrees otherwise or you have a fit note.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device, including a laptop, must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it is missing. Reporting quickly allows the device to be wiped remotely.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you become ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and the annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following section 2 of the Sickness Absence Policy. The passages do not say how the fit note requirement applies to sickness of 7 days or fewer, which section 3 covers only for absences outside annual leave.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Do not report suspected money laundering in SafeLog and do not discuss it with the customer or with colleagues who do not need to know. Instead, complete the internal suspicious activity report form and send it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) on the same day, as described in the Compliance Guidelines. Do not investigate yourself, and do not tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees cannot be claimed on expenses. They are paid directly by the company under the Training and Development Policy (P1 §6), and the Expenses Policy specifically excludes training course fees from claims (P2 §6). Travel and accommodation for approved training can be claimed under the Expenses Policy (P1 §6).

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor, so someone who looks under 18 must not be allowed on it. Think 25 applies as well: anyone who appears to be under 25 must show valid photo ID. The passages do not say what to do if the person is already on the floor or refuses to leave, or who to escalate to.

question: I was off sick for months last year and couldn't use my leave. How much can I carry over and by when?
expected_answer: Up to 20 days because of long-term sickness, to be used within 18 months of the end of that leave year.
ai_answer: If long-term sickness stopped you from taking your leave, you may carry forward up to 20 days, not the usual 8. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned. The passages do not define "long-term sickness", so whether your absence qualifies is not settled by them. Without that exception, the standard limit is 8 days, which must be used by 30 June of the new leave year.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: No, not as a single block. Between 24 December and 1 January (a peak period), gaming floor and security employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave, and only with approval from their venue's General Manager [P2]. Leave requests must be made through StaffHub at least twice the length of the leave requested, so a 5-day request needs 10 days' notice [P3]. The passages do not say whether two weeks could be split into separate shorter blocks over Christmas, or how the rota notice rules interact with the peak-period limit beyond the cover condition, so check with your General Manager.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: You must give notice of at least twice the length of the leave requested, so for a full week (7 days) of leave, request it at least 14 days before the first day of leave. Requests made after the rota is published (gaming floor and security rotas are published 4 weeks in advance) can only be approved if cover is available. Managers should respond within 5 working days.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: You can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year without needing approval, and those days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year or they are lost and not paid. You can carry forward more than 8 days (up to 20 days) only in limited cases: long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where your manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved the exception in writing. Days carried forward due to sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned; other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June. The passages do not say how the Employee Handbook's 28-day entitlement interacts with these carry-forward rules beyond referring booking and carry-forward to the Annual Leave Policy.

question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
ai_answer: Employees in office-based support roles (such as Finance, HR, IT, Compliance and Marketing) may work remotely for up to 2 days a week, with their line manager's agreement. Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days, when office-based employees are expected to be in the office unless they are on leave or have agreed otherwise with their manager.

question: Am I allowed to work from abroad for a few days?
expected_answer: Office-based staff can, for up to 10 working days a year, with manager and Information Security approval in advance.
ai_answer: Yes, but only in limited circumstances. Employees in office-based support roles may work from outside the UK for up to 10 working days in a calendar year. This must be approved in advance by your line manager and by the Information Security team, and the request must be made through the IT Service Desk at least 2 weeks before travel. The passages do not say whether this rule applies to employees in other roles, such as venue staff.
